````text
1: # rsynxiety
2: 
3: Copying terabytes of video files between hard drives requires care. Transfers can fail halfway through. A bad sector can corrupt a file during transit.
4: 
5: `rsynxiety` is a Node.js CLI wrapper for rsync. It defaults to strict verification settings to verify the files.
6: 
7: ## Installation
8: 
9: We use pnpm.
10: 
11: ```bash
12: git clone <repository>
13: cd rsynxiety
14: pnpm install
15: pnpm link --global
16: ```
17: 
18: ## Usage
19: 
20: Run the tool without arguments to open the interactive wizard.
21: 
22: ```bash
23: rsynxiety
24: ```
25: 
26: Or pass the paths directly.
27: 
28: ```bash
29: rsynxiety /Volumes/SourceDrive /Volumes/DestDrive
30: ```
31: 
32: Use `--canary .drive_id` to strictly require a sentinel file on the destination. Use `--skip-hash` to skip the final xxHash verification.
33: 
34: ## Architecture and design decisions
35: 
36: Hard drives fail. Cables come loose. `rsynxiety` handles these interruptions.
37: 
38: ### Partial transfers
39: 
40: When a transfer drops midway, you need a way to resume it. Rsync provides two common flags for this. They are `--append-verify` and `--partial-dir`.
41: 
42: We use `--partial-dir`. When an initial transfer breaks, this flag keeps the incomplete file hidden in a dot folder. A subsequent run resumes the file from this isolated directory and only moves it into the final destination when it completes. 
43: 
44: Using `--append-verify` appends data directly to the incomplete file at the destination path and verifies the old data matches. We avoid this flag. It leaves partial files sitting in the open where other programs might try to read them. It also skips files entirely if the destination size matches the source size, even if the bytes are different. This can cause silent data loss on interrupted pre-allocated files.
45: 
46: ### Hardware cache flushing
47: 
48: Operating systems hold data in memory caches to speed up apparent write times. If a script reads a file right after writing it, the kernel serves the file from RAM. This can mask disk controller errors.
49: 
50: We run the `sync` command before we hash files. This forces the OS to flush all pending buffers to the physical storage media. When we calculate the final checksum, we read the actual bits off the disk hardware to verify the write succeeded.
The above content does NOT show the entire file contents. If you need to view any lines of the file which were not shown to complete your task, call this tool again to view those lines.
````
